title: Indices, Logarithm and Surds Quiz 9
description: Combine the logs, solve, then check the domain. Some roots will not survive.
instructions: Indices, Logarithm and Surds: Solving logarithmic equations.
Write maths answers with the keypad. Any equal form is accepted.
Every question has a trap. Slow down at the signs.

questions.question: Solve $\log_5(2x+4)=2$.
questions.explanation: $2x+4=5^2=25$, so $x=10.5$. Watch out: $\log_5(\ldots)=2$ means the bracket equals $25$, not $10$.

questions.question: Solve $\log x=1-\log(x-3)$ (base $10$).
questions.explanation: $\log x+\log(x-3)=1$ gives $x(x-3)=10$, so $x^2-3x-10=0$ and $x=5$ or $x=-2$. Watch out: the domain needs $x>3$, so $x=-2$ is rejected.

questions.question: Solve $\log_2(x^{2}-6x)=3+\log_2(1-x)$.
questions.explanation: $x^2-6x=8(1-x)$ gives $x^2+2x-8=0$, so $x=2$ or $x=-4$. The domain needs $1-x>0$, so $x=2$ is rejected. Watch out: check **both** logs; only $x=-4$ works.

questions.question: Solve $2\log_9(\sqrt{x})-\log_9(6x-1)=0$.
questions.explanation: $2\log_9\sqrt x=\log_9x$, so $x=6x-1$ and $x=\dfrac15$. Check: $6x-1=0.2>0$. Watch out: $2\log_9\sqrt{x}=\log_9x$, not $\log_9 2x$.

questions.question: Solve $\ln10-\ln(7-x)=\ln x$. Give all the solutions.
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{10}{7-x}=x$ gives $x^2-7x+10=0$, so $x=2$ or $x=5$. Both satisfy $0<x<7$. Watch out: both roots are valid here, so check before you reject.

questions.question: Solve $\log x+\log(x-1)=\log(3x+12)$.
questions.explanation: $x(x-1)=3x+12$ gives $x^2-4x-12=0$, so $x=6$ or $x=-2$. The domain needs $x>1$. Watch out: $x=-2$ is rejected because $\log(-2)$ does not exist.

questions.question: After solving a logarithm equation, every answer must be checked in the original equation.
questions.explanation: Combining logs can introduce roots that make an argument negative. Watch out: the check is part of the solution.

questions.question: Solve $\log x+\log(x-3)=1$. One step is wrong. Tap it.
questions.explanation: $x=-2$ makes $\log x$ undefined, so only $x=5$ is a solution. Watch out: factorising gives two roots, but the domain keeps one.

questions.question: Solve $\ln x+\ln(x-2)=\ln3$. One step is wrong. Tap it, then choose the correct step.
questions.explanation: Adding logs multiplies the arguments: $\ln[x(x-2)]=\ln3$. Watch out: $\ln a+\ln b=\ln(ab)$, not $\ln(a+b)$.

questions.question: For which values of $x$ is $\log_2(x-1)$ defined?
questions.explanation: We need $x-1>0$, so $x>1$: $2$, $5$ and $10$ work. Watch out: $x=1$ gives $\log_2 0$, which is undefined.

questions.question: Solve $\log_3x=-2$.
questions.explanation: $x=3^{-2}=\dfrac19$. Watch out: a negative logarithm means a number between $0$ and $1$, so $x$ is a fraction, not $-6$.

questions.assertion: $\log_2 x$ is defined for every real number $x$.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false: $\log_2x$ needs $x>0$. The reason is true, and it is exactly why $x$ must be positive. Watch out: the reason is true but it contradicts the assertion.
